text.p: Fashion designer Donna Karan was greeted with great fanfare when the company made its debut on Wall Street last summer, but the stock's future now looks more precarious.

Donna Karan stock lost more than 15 percent of its value Tuesday after the company warned that losses at its troubled beauty division hurt its third quarter profits and were likely to also cut its fourth-quarter profits to break-even.
Donna Karan's shares, which were launched in a public offering in June, were off $2.875 at $15.875 in late afternoon trading, and led the list of loss leaders on the New York Stock Exchange.
Several analysts, including Morgan Stanley, also cut their 1996 and 1997 earnings estimates for the company.

Late on Monday, New York-based Donna Karan said it earned $13 million, or 61 cents a share, in the third quarter, up from year-ago earnings of $11.8 million, or 52 cents. Sales rose to $173.4 million from $152.3 million.

The company forecast break-even fourth-quarter results because current projections for sales in its beauty division continue to be below target and the unit is expected to lose $900,000 for the quarter.

Donna Karan launched a public offering of 10.75 million shares on June 28, in its second try to go public. The first attempt in 1993 was called off because a drop in sales depressed its offering price.
